text:
miriam: Quick sync — I want to land an RBAC tweak for the onprem keystore-sync service. Goal: allow it to call our KMS only for key-rotation and export-checks, not decrypt customer data. Questions: audit logging fields we need, netpol implications, and can we avoid direct KMS egress from worker nodes?
aj: +1 on limiting scope. Prefer a KMS-proxy sidecar that authenticates service identity and enforces operation ACLs. That way nodes never hold KMS creds. Also suggest mTLS to the proxy and proxy to KMS.
sam_k: Netpol: deny-by-default for app namespaces. Only allow egress to the keystore-proxy svc on port 8443, and proxy -> bom-kms on the control plane subnet. Example NetworkPolicy to start:```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-keystore-proxy-egress
  namespace: keystore
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-sync
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          infra: true
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: keystore-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8443
```
Also add hostNetwork=false, run as non-root.
sec-bot: AUTOMATED SCAN: keystore-lib v1.2.3 has known issue (CVE-2025-0100) - affects local key export API. Recommend upgrade to v1.2.5 or apply advisory patch. See https://sec.example/cve/CVE-2025-0100
olivia: For audit logs we need stable fields for SIEM: timestamp, request_id, principal_id, principal_ssp (service/sa), operation (Encrypt/Decrypt/Rotate/Export), key_id, result (ALLOW/DENY), from_ip, vpc_id, tenant_id. Prefer structured JSON logs and a short human message for oncall. Example log line:```json
{"ts":"2025-06-12T14:23:11Z","req_id":"req-9f7a","principal":"svc-keystore-sync","op":"Rotate","key_id":"projects/px/keys/rw-k1","result":"ALLOW","vpc":"vpc-pri-42","tenant":"cust-123"}
```
miriam: Good. Two clarifications: 1) we should not allow keystore-sync to issue Decrypt on production keys; only Rotate/Sign/Describe. 2) How do we prove no data egress in a compliance audit?
aj: For audit proof, capture per-request flow: pod -> proxy -> kms, and record the proxy's outbound IPs and TLS peer certs. Keep packet-capture for a short retention (sensitive) and provide hash of captures as tamper-evidence. Also publish a small attestation artifact (signed statement + log anchor) to the customer-specific audit bucket.
sam_k: Also enable eBPF conntrack observability on nodes (read-only) so infra can show no external 3rd-party IPs were hit. That helps compliance.
dinesh: On vuln triage / incident playbook: if CVE exploited or odd export activity detected: 1) lock key usage: set KMS deny policy for affected key(s), 2) rotate keys (create new key & rewrap), 3) revoke service account tokens for keystore-sync, 4) fail over to software keystore (local ephemeral) for limited window, 5) notify customers per SLA, 6) preserve logs and create forensic bundle. Keep runbook steps minimal and scriptable.
miriam: Can we do automated canary for RBAC change? I want a rollout that 1) enables proxy mode but denies decrypt ops for 5% of clusters, 2) monitor audit events for unexpected DENY spikes, 3) auto rollback on anomalies.
aj: Yes — use an ingress label based rollout: keystore-proxy:canary=true for small set; route sync pods from those clusters to proxy.canary. Hook alerts on: any rpc with op=="Decrypt" returning ALLOW, and any >5x baseline DENY in 10m.
sec-bot: POLICY CHECK: proposed RBAC change suggests granting kms.keys.get on project scope. Recommendation: narrow to specific key resource, add condition: request.auth.claims.service == "svc-keystore-sync".
olivia: One more logging note — include a short hashed prompt/trace id linking back to application request so we can correlate service-level events w/o leaking PII. Use stable HMAC key stored in the keystore (rotate monthly).
sam_k: Operational checklist before deploy: - proxy sidecar image scanned & pinned - netpol in place - egress gateway validated - observability hooks (ebpf + proxy logs) - SIEM mapping done - canary cluster list prepared
dinesh: Incident contact list + playbook snippet (for runbook vault):```text
1) Triage oncall (sec lead) @channel
2) Revoke SA tokens: gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable || kubectl delete secrets svc-token-keystore
3) Apply KMS deny-policy (console CLI)
4) Rotate keys & rewrap
5) Forensic bundle: collect /var/log/proxy/*.log, audit.log, network policy traces
```
miriam: Great — I'll open a PR with the narrow RBAC binding + proxy helm chart and include the runbook + SIEM field mapping. Ping me for review. :thumbsup:
